# Capability Loss -- Hook-Removal Change Set (2026-08-01)

Orphaned-code analysis (impact_analysis_graph.json) answers "what code stops being
reachable." This file answers "what stops working" -- one entry per lost capability,
by name, with its current owner file and the requirement it maps to in SRS.md.

SRS.md FR-9 ("Hook System") names `hooks/pre-tool-enforcer.py`, `hooks/post-tool-tracker.py`
and `hooks/stop-notifier.py` as its Key Scripts, with acceptance criterion: "All four hook
events fire, and a blocking policy returns exit code 2 from the PreToolUse hook so the tool
call does not proceed." Deleting the PreToolUse and PostToolUse entries makes that acceptance
criterion FALSE for two of the four events -- this is a direct FR-9 regression, not just an
orphaned-code footnote.

## PreToolUse capabilities lost (hooks/pre_tool_enforcer/, 74 nodes + 14-node shim)

| Capability | Owner file | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Task-breakdown-pending block (blocks Write/Edit/Bash until task list exists) | policies/task_breakdown.py | FR-9 |
| Skill/agent-selection-pending block | policies/skill_selection.py | FR-9 |
| Review-checkpoint block (blocks code-changing tools mid-review) | policies/checkpoint.py | FR-9 |
| Context-read-gate (blocks Write/Edit/NotebookEdit/Bash until context files read) | policies/context_read.py | FR-9 |
| Level-1-sync-gate | policies/level1_sync.py | FR-9 |
| Windows-only-shell-command detection + branch protection | policies/bash_commands.py | FR-9, NFR-5 |
| Python/Windows cp1252 Unicode-crash detection | policies/python_unicode.py | FR-9, NFR-5 |
| Known-failure-pattern lookup (failure-kb.json) | policies/failure_kb.py | FR-9, NFR-3 |
| Grep content-mode head_limit enforcement | policies/grep_opt.py | FR-9 |
| Read large-file offset/limit enforcement | policies/read_opt.py | FR-9 |
| Write/Edit tool-optimization hints | policies/write_edit.py | FR-9 |
| General-purpose subagent persona gate | policies/agent_persona.py | FR-9 |

| **Version-push gate** -- blocks `git push` without a VERSION bump on the branch, and blocks push with an unclean tree (the bypass this repo's own commit history records fixing: `1bb4303 "close a bypass in the version push rule"`) | policies/push_gate.py | FR-9, rules/44 (SRS lifecycle), rules/11 |
| Warm-daemon fast path -- keeps a long-lived process so PreToolUse checks skip cold Python-interpreter startup on every tool call | daemon.py (`ensure_daemon_running`, `run_daemon`, `try_daemon_fast_path`) | NFR-1 (Performance) |
| PolicyRegistry -- ordered, fail-open policy-check dispatch used by all 14 policies above | registry.py | FR-9 (mechanism) |

All 14 policy checks plus the daemon and registry mechanism that runs them go dark
together -- PreToolUse stops firing at all (settings.json entry removed), so nothing in
this table executes irrespective of the internal package structure.

## PostToolUse capabilities lost (hooks/post_tool_tracker/, 32 nodes + 7-node shim)

| Capability | Owner file | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Session progress/checkpoint state (progress delta dict, session file I/O) -- this is the writer behind NFR-3's "Checkpoint recovery: pipeline can resume from any step after crash" | progress_tracker.py | **NFR-3 (Reliability)** |
| Tool-usage metrics tracking (per-tool counts, timing) | core.py (`track_tool_usage` path) | NFR-3 |
| Phase-complexity enforcement | policies/phase_complexity.py | FR-9 |
| Post-merge VERSION/doc sync trigger | policies/post_merge_update.py | FR-9, rules/44/45/46 |
| Skill-selection flag clearing (Level 3.5) | policies/skill_selection_clear.py | FR-9 |
| Task-breakdown flag clearing (Level 3.1) | policies/task_breakdown_clear.py | FR-9 |
| Task-update-frequency warning | policies/task_tracking.py | FR-9 |
| Uncommitted-push policy (Level 3.11) | policies/uncommitted_push.py | FR-9 |
| Auto-close GitHub issues on task completion | github_integration.py (`close_github_issues_on_completion`) | FR-4 (integration lifecycle) |

This is the **NFR-3 finding**: post-tool-tracker.py is the sole writer of session
progress/checkpoint state and per-tool metrics. With PostToolUse removed from
settings.json, `session-progress.json` and tool-usage counters stop being updated on every
turn -- NFR-3's "resume from any step after crash" guarantee degrades to whatever state was
last written before the hook was disabled, and Step 8 (Final Telemetry & Summary Report)
loses its primary input.

## Cross-cutting capability lost (hooks/policy_tracking_helper.py, 8 nodes)

| Capability | Owner file | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Policy-execution recording (feeds the policy-enforcement MCP server's flow-trace aggregate) | policy_tracking_helper.py (`record_policy_execution`, `record_sub_operation`) | NFR-3 |
| Flow-trace summary retrieval | policy_tracking_helper.py (`get_flow_trace_summary`) | NFR-3 |

Verdict (see impact_analysis_graph.json for the evidence): this file has no production
importer outside `hooks/pre_tool_enforcer/core.py` and `hooks/post_tool_tracker/core.py`.
Both of those callers are themselves being deleted, so this capability goes dark as a
direct consequence even though `policy_tracking_helper.py` is not itself one of the three
named deletion targets in the settings.json change set.

## NOT lost (verified, do not re-flag)

- Session identity/path resolution (`ide_paths.py`, `project_session.py`,
  `session_context.py`) -- confirmed independent production importers outside the three
  doomed packages (`scripts/github_pr_workflow/git_ops.py`,
  `scripts/github_operations/issue_manager.py`,
  `scripts/github_operations/session_integration.py` import `ide_paths`;
  `ide_paths.py` itself imports `project_session`; `langgraph_engine/context_sync/helpers.py`
  and `scripts/helpers/session_resolver.py` import `session_context` directly). These
  survive hook deletion unchanged.
- Stop-hook capabilities (session-end maintenance, voice notification, auto-PR workflow) --
  the Stop hook is RETAINED per the change set; see stop_hook_overhead.md for its separate
  overhead audit. No capability loss here, only a per-turn cost question.
- `scripts/3-level-flow.py` (UserPromptSubmit) going off the hot path is a **behavior
  change**, not a capability loss in the orphaned-code sense: the file is not deleted and
  remains directly runnable; the call graph shows no edges into it from the three deleted
  packages either way. Its capability (automatic per-prompt pipeline entry) is lost from
  the *automatic* trigger path but remains available as a manual invocation.
